rules.title: Omi rules
lesson1.title: Meet the cards
lesson1.goal: The 32 cards, the 4 suits and the rank order
lesson1.e1: Hello! 👋 Omi is played with 32 cards: take a normal deck and remove the cards from 2 to 6.
lesson1.e2: There are 4 suits: [S] Spades, [H] Hearts, [D] Diamonds and [C] Clubs. Hearts and Diamonds are red. Spades and Clubs are black.
lesson1.e3: Each suit has 8 cards. From the highest to the lowest: [AS] [KS] [QS] [JS] [10S] [9S] [8S] [7S]
lesson1.e4: A is the Ace, K the King, Q the Queen and J the Jack. The Ace is the highest card and the 7 is the lowest. The order is the same in every suit.
lesson1.k3: One more. Which card is the highest?
lesson1.k4: Last one! Tap the highest card.
lesson1.retry: That's not the highest. Remember the order: A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7.
lesson1.e5: Well done! 🎉 Now you know the cards. Remember: A > K > Q > J > 10 > 9 > 8 > 7.
lesson1.q1.x: The Ace (A) is the highest card in every suit.
lesson1.q2: How many cards are used in Omi?
lesson1.q2.x: Omi uses 32 cards: 4 suits with 8 cards each, from A down to 7.
lesson1.q3.x: The King (K) is higher than the Queen (Q). J, 10 and 7 are all lower than the Queen.
lesson2.title: Follow suit
lesson2.goal: The rule: play the suit that was led
lesson2.e1: In every trick, one player plays the first card. They may play any suit. Everyone else must then play that same suit. This is called following suit.
lesson2.e2: Look at the table. You sit at the bottom and your partner sits at the top. The two opponents sit on either side. Play goes anticlockwise: right, top, left, then you.
lesson2.b1: The player on the right leads [KH]. Now everyone must play [H] Hearts.
lesson2.p1: Your turn. [H] Hearts were led, and you have Hearts. Play a Heart.
lesson2.e3: Right! You had [H] Hearts, so you had to play one. The player who played [AH] won this trick. The trick winner leads the next trick.
lesson2.b2: Now the player on the left leads [KD].
lesson2.p2: [D] Diamonds were led, and you have no Diamonds! When that happens, you may play any card. Choose any card.
lesson2.e4: Remember: if you have the suit that was led, you must play it. If you don't, you may play any card.
lesson2.q1: [H] Hearts were led. You have [9H] and [AS]. Which must you play?
lesson2.q1.x: You have a Heart, so you must play [9H]. [AS] is higher, but you can't play it.
lesson2.q2: [C] Clubs were led and you have no Clubs. What can you play?
lesson2.q2.x: Without the suit that was led, you may play any card. You can't skip your turn.
lesson2.q3: [S] Spades were led. You have Spades, but you'd like to play a high Heart. Can you?
lesson2.q3.b: No, I must play a Spade
lesson2.q3.x: If you have the suit that was led, you must play it.
lesson3.title: Winning a trick
lesson3.goal: The highest card of the suit led wins
lesson3.e1: A trick is one turn where all four players play one card each. If no trump is played, the player with the highest card of the suit led wins the trick.
lesson3.e2: A card of another suit can't win, however high it is (even an Ace). (Trumps come in the next lesson.)
lesson3.b1: Your partner has no [D] Diamonds. They play [AC].
lesson3.k1: Who wins this trick? Tap the winning card.
lesson3.r2: Not quite. [D] Diamonds were led, so find the highest Diamond. [AC] is another suit, so it doesn't count.
lesson3.e3: Right! [KD] won. [AC] is high, but it's a [C] Club, so it can't win. Now the player on the right leads the next trick.
lesson3.b2: The player on the right leads [9H].
lesson3.b3: The player on the left has no [H] Hearts. They play [AD].
lesson3.p2: Your only Heart is [8H]. Play it.
lesson3.r3: Not quite. [H] Hearts were led. Which is the highest Heart?
lesson3.e4: Well done! Your partner won with [JH]. A trick your partner wins belongs to your team.
lesson3.q1: Trumps are [S]. [9C] was led, then [AH], [QC] and [10C] were played. Which card wins?
lesson3.q1.x: Clubs were led, and the highest Club is [QC]. [AH] is another suit.
lesson3.q2: A player without the suit led plays [AD]. [D] is not trumps. Can that card win the trick?
lesson3.q2.x: A card of another suit never wins, even an Ace. Only a trump can do that.
lesson3.q3: What does the trick winner do next?
lesson3.q3.x: The trick winner leads the next trick.
lesson4.title: Trumps
lesson4.goal: A trump beats any card of another suit
lesson4.e1: In every round, one suit is trumps: the suit with special power for that round. This round, trumps are [H] Hearts. You can see it at the top.
lesson4.e2: A trump beats any card of another suit. Even a small [7H] beats [AS]!
lesson4.e3: But remember: if you have the suit that was led, you must play it. You can only trump when you don't have that suit.
lesson4.b1: The player on the right leads [AS].
lesson4.p1: You have no [S] Spades! Play a trump ([H]) to win this trick.
lesson4.r1: Play a trump ([H]) to win this trick.
lesson4.e4: Well done! You trumped it. Even [AS] loses to your trump. Now you lead the next trick.
lesson4.p2: This time, let's lead a trump. Play a [H] Heart.
lesson4.e5: When trumps are led, the others must play trumps too (if they have them), and the highest trump wins. If two players trump, the higher trump wins.
lesson4.q1: Trumps are [H]. [AS], [7H], [KS] and [QS] are played. Which card wins?
lesson4.q1.x: [7H] is a trump. A trump beats any card of another suit.
lesson4.q2: Trumps are [D]. [AC] is led, then [9D], [KC] and [JD] are played. Which card wins?
lesson4.q2.x: Two trumps were played. The higher one is [JD], so it wins.
lesson4.q3: [S] Spades were led. You have Spades and a trump. Can you trump?
lesson4.q3.a: No, I must play a Spade
lesson4.q3.x: If you have the suit that was led, you must play it. You can only trump when you don't have that suit.
lesson5.title: Choosing trumps
lesson5.goal: Look at your first 4 cards and choose good trumps
lesson5.e1: In every round, the dealer first deals 4 cards to each player. The player to the dealer's right looks at those 4 cards and chooses trumps. Nobody may help. Then everyone gets 4 more cards.
lesson5.e2: Here's how to choose good trumps: ① Look for the suit you have the most of. ② Look for suits with high cards like A, K, Q and J. The suit with more cards and high cards is the best choice.
lesson5.t1: It's your turn to choose trumps. Look at your 4 cards and choose the best trumps.
lesson5.r1: Look again. Which suit do you have the most of? The bars below can help.
lesson5.e3: Right! You have 3 [H] Hearts, including high cards like [KH] and [QH].
lesson5.t2: 4 new cards. This time you have 2 Clubs and 2 Hearts. Which are the best trumps?
lesson5.r2: The counts are equal. Then choose the suit with the high cards.
lesson5.e4: Right! When the counts are equal, the suit with high cards like [AC] and [KC] is better. Those cards can win tricks.
lesson5.t3: Last one! Choose the best trumps.
lesson5.r3: Three cards of one suit are worth more than a single high card. Look again.
lesson5.e5: Well done! With 3 [D] Diamonds as trumps you can win several tricks. A suit with just one [KS] is too weak for trumps.
lesson5.q1: Your 4 cards: [AS] [JS] [9H] [7D]. Which are the best trumps?
lesson5.q1.x: You have 2 Spades, including high cards like [AS] and [JS].
lesson5.q2.b: The player to the dealer's right
lesson5.q2.x: The player to the dealer's right chooses trumps and leads the first trick.
lesson5.q3: Can you help your partner choose trumps?
lesson5.q3.x: The trump chooser must decide alone, looking only at their own 4 cards.
lesson6.title: Points
lesson6.e1: A round has 8 tricks. The team that wins 5 or more tricks wins the round and gets points.
lesson6.e2: We chose trumps and won 6 tricks. When the trump-choosing team wins, it gets {trumpWin} point(s).
lesson6.e3: This time we chose trumps, but they won 5 tricks. When the team that did not choose trumps wins, it gets {defWin} point(s)!
lesson6.c1: They chose trumps and won 6 tricks. How many points do they get?
lesson6.r1: They chose trumps. Remember how many points the trump-choosing team gets for a win.
lesson6.c2: They chose trumps, but we won 5 tricks. How many points do we get?
lesson6.r2: We didn't choose trumps. The team that didn't choose trumps gets more points for a win.
lesson6.e4: If one team wins all 8 tricks, that's කැපෝති (Kapothi)! 🎉 Kapothi is worth {kapothi} point(s), whoever chose trumps.
lesson6.e5: If the tricks are 4–4, the round is a tie. Nobody gets points, but the team that wins the next round gets {tieBonus} extra point(s).
lesson6.e6: In the round after the tie, we chose trumps and won 5 tricks. We get {trumpWin} point(s) plus {tieBonus} tie-bonus point(s).
lesson6.e7: The first team to reach {target} points wins the game. 🏆
lesson6.q1: The trump-choosing team won 6 tricks. How many points?
lesson6.q1.x: When the trump-choosing team wins 5–7 tricks, it gets {trumpWin} point(s).
lesson6.q2.x: Winning all 8 tricks is Kapothi. It's worth {kapothi} point(s).
lesson6.q3.b: Nobody scores. The next round's winner gets {tieBonus} extra point(s)
lesson6.q3.c: The same round is played again
lesson6.q3.x: In a tie nobody scores. The team that wins the next round gets {tieBonus} extra point(s).
lesson7.title: Playing with your partner
lesson7.goal: Don't beat your partner. Lead the suit your partner doesn't have.
lesson7.e1: Omi is a team game. You and your partner win tricks together, and a trick your partner wins belongs to your team. This round, trumps are [S] Spades.
lesson7.b1: The player on the left leads [KD].
lesson7.p1: You have [D] Diamonds. Play a Diamond.
lesson7.b2: Look! Your partner has no [D] Diamonds. They trump it ([S]) and win the trick.
lesson7.e2: Now we know your partner has no [D] Diamonds. Remember this. It will be useful later!
lesson7.b3: Your partner leads [AC]. [AC] is the highest Club.
lesson7.p2: You have [KC] and [8C]. Which do you play?
lesson7.r2: Your partner's [AC] is already winning. Don't waste [KC]. Play the low card.
lesson7.e3: Right! Don't play high cards on a trick your partner is winning. You saved [KC] to win a later trick.
lesson7.b5: An opponent played [KH]. Now they are winning.
lesson7.p3: Your partner is losing. Can you take this trick?
lesson7.r3: The opponents are winning with [KH]. Take the trick with your [AH].
lesson7.e4: Well done! You took the trick when your partner was losing. Now you lead.
lesson7.p4: Remember that your partner has no [D] Diamonds? Which suit is best to lead?
lesson7.r4: Your partner has no [D] Diamonds. If you lead a Diamond, they can trump it.
lesson7.e5: Well done! You led a Diamond and your partner trumped it to win. 🎉 Lead a suit your partner doesn't have, so they can trump it.
lesson7.q1: Your partner played [AC]. You have [KC] and [8C]. Which should you play?
lesson7.q1.x: Your partner is already winning. Play [8C] and save [KC] for a later trick.
lesson7.q2: Earlier, your partner trumped a trick when [H] Hearts were led. Now you lead. Which suit is best?
lesson7.q2.x: Your partner has no Hearts. If you lead Hearts, they can trump again.
lesson7.q3: Your partner is winning this trick and you don't have the suit that was led. What do you play?
lesson7.q3.x: Your partner is already winning, so there's no need to trump. Play your least useful card.
lesson8.title: Remembering cards
lesson8.goal: The highest cards left, missing suits and counting trumps
lesson8.e1: Good Omi players remember the cards that have been played. That tells you which high cards are left and who has run out of a suit. This round, trumps are [H] Hearts.
lesson8.b1: The player on the right leads [AS].
lesson8.p1: [AS] is winning. Your Spades can't win this trick. Play your lowest Spade.
lesson8.r1: You can't win this trick. Save your high cards and play your lowest Spade, [8S].
lesson8.e2: This is the card tracker. Played cards are greyed out. [AS] and [KS] are gone, so your [QS] is now the highest Spade left. The ★ marks it.
lesson8.b2: The player on the right leads [9D].
lesson8.b3: The player on the left doesn't play a Diamond. They trump it with [8H]!
lesson8.p2: Your only Diamond is [7D]. Play it.
lesson8.e3: The player on the left didn't play a [D] Diamond, so they have no Diamonds at all. If Diamonds are led again, they will trump. Remember that.
lesson8.e4: You can count trumps too. There are 8 trumps. Look at ‘Trumps left’ in the tracker. Take away the trumps in your own hand, and you know how many the others still have.
lesson8.b4: The player on the left leads [AC].
lesson8.p3: Your only Club is [9C]. Play it.
lesson8.k1: [AC] and [KC] are gone. Which is now the highest Club left? Check the tracker and tap it.
lesson8.r2: Look at the Clubs row in the tracker. Which is the highest card not played yet?
lesson8.e5: Well done! 🎉 [AC] and [KC] are gone, so [QC] is now the highest Club. Remember the highest cards left, and you can use them to win tricks.
lesson8.q1: [AS] and [KS] have been played. You have [QS]. Which is now the highest Spade left?
lesson8.q1.x: The A and K are gone. Of the Spades left, [QS] is the highest.
lesson8.q2: Earlier, when [C] Clubs were led, an opponent played a Diamond. What does that tell us?
lesson8.q2.x: You must follow suit if you can. They didn't play a Club, so they have none.
lesson8.q3: Trumps are [H]. 5 Hearts have been played and you hold 2. How many Hearts do the others still have?
lesson8.q3.x: There are 8 Hearts. 8 − 5 − 2 = 1. Just one is left.
